questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important to me that I would learn about the pharmaceutical industry outside of Europe, since I wanted to know the industry beyond the European pharmacopeia, and thus choosing a country in Asia was prioritized.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The host university was very helpful in giving guidelines upon arrival and thus the information needed was provided.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received assistance from the international office on campus, the housing office as well as from local students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are dorms on the campus, which are easy to sign up for. You sign up to be allocated a dorm room when you apply for the university. If you don't wish to live in the dorms, the university will provide you with a list of other possible accommodations off campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are no meal plans on the university, however there are many cafeterias also in the dorm building, and there are semi equipped kitchen in which you can cook food.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Be aware to buy your own utensils and maybe even cleaning appliances as there may only be pots and pans to cook with and no utensils or dishes to eat with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was fairly straight forward. Once you enter the application page you just fill out all the information and provide a photo of yourself for the student ID card. The application page is letter used as a communication portal where the university will provide you with information throughout the semester. Furthermore you will also find your acceptance letter on the application page in the top right corner.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I used the student councilor as a means of help, otherwise they are also able to contact the host university should a problem occur.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I successfully registered to all the courses I wanted, but I only got a spot because I wrote to two of the professors and they allowed me in even after the registration period.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The registration process is super competitive so be really prepared. The way you can prepare is by first having more preapproved courses than what you plan to sign up for, so that in case you couldn't sign up for the courses you wanted, you can sign up for some other courses that you know your home university has approved of. Secondly, remember to write down both the course name and course code, so that when the registration starts you can quickly find your courses. If you didn't get to register to the courses you wanted you can always try again in the "add and drop" period, or you can write to the professor of the course and ask them if there are any available spots, since the professor usually expands the capacity of the course after the registration period.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Although I was a master student at KU I applied to be accepted as an undergraduate student at my host university after being allowed to do so by KU. So the courses I had was undergraduate courses however they were on a high academic level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is a bit different than that at KU. The lectures were mandatory and there both midterms and finals, so the workload is a bit hard but the environment of which you learn is really good, so you get motivated to study.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Functional neuroanatomy (Department of brain and cognitive sciences)
Learning and memory (Department of brain and cognitive sciences)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend you take courses that you really are passionate about and that also fall in line with your major at KU.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There is a national health insurance that you must pay as a citizen in Korea. This must be paid every month after receiving your foreign registration card. The insurance is a little high but is mandatory so be aware to account for this in your budget.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is really cheap, and often times it can cost less to eat out rather than buy groceries and cooking yourself as some groceries are quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are all sorts of cultural, athletic and social activities and clubs at Ewha however I didn't participate in any of them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommed to be part of the peace-buddy program as a lot of information is shared in the group chats and there are a lot of different activities hosted by the buddies.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Seoul as much as possible. Seoul is such a lovely city and there is so much to see and do!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to adjust to the local culture as long as you are respectful of the differences and try not to make a big deal out of it.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be prepared to not talk to loudly in public spaces, and not to have phone calls on the train or even talk loudly on the train, as this is seen as rude.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate how kind, social and welcoming Koreans are. There is a huge social scene in Seoul and thus even when being alone, it is really easy to socialize with strangers and make friends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy your stay, don't stress too much and don't bring too much clothes as you might need the space for the clothes and things you are gonna buy in Korea.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for the cold winter in both February and March, but also be prepared to have some lighter clothes since after May the temperatures are really high (higher than in Denmark).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing Seoul and making so many new friends has been the most rewarding part of my exchange experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge is balancing life outside of the university and also the time you spent on studying. Sometimes it is needed of you to just study all day, and it can be hard to both do that and also have time outside of the university, so remember to balance it well.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
